title: Connect the Dots: Constellations
objective: After this level you can explain what a constellation is and why its stars usually aren’t near each other.
summary: There are 88 official constellations covering the sky. Their stars only line up from our viewpoint.

cards.headline: Orion isn't really a hunter, and his stars aren't even neighbors.
cards.body: A constellation is a picture we see from one spot in space: Earth. So what's actually up there?

cards.headline: From pictures to borders
cards.body: People have long joined up the stars into patterns and named them after figures, animals and objects. Today astronomers go further: the sky is divided into 88 official constellations, each one a region with set boundaries, like countries on a map. Together they cover the whole sky, so every star lands in some constellation, even the ones that aren't part of any picture.

cards.headline: A trick of perspective
cards.body: Stars that look side by side can be very different distances from Earth. Remember light-years from Level 8? One star in a pattern could be a few dozen light-years away, its neighbor hundreds. They only look close together from where we stand, the way a faraway streetlight can seem to sit right next to your neighbor's porch light.

cards.fact: The Big Dipper is not a constellation.
cards.context: It's an asterism: a familiar star pattern that isn't one of the official constellations. The Dipper is part of the constellation Ursa Major, the Great Bear. So if you've ever spotted the saucepan, congratulations: you've also seen part of a bear.

cards.headline: Constellations: decoded
learned: Constellations began as named star patterns
Their stars are usually far apart in space
The Big Dipper is an asterism in Ursa Major

questions.prompt: How many official constellations are there?

options.rationale: That’s the number of zodiac signs; the constellations cover the whole sky.

questions.explanation: Astronomers officially recognize 88 constellations, which together cover the entire sky.

questions.prompt: Two stars sit side by side in the same constellation. What’s most likely true?

options.label: They may be very different distances from Earth
They orbit each other
options.rationale: Some stars do, but most constellation stars are unrelated.

options.label: They are the same distance from Earth
options.rationale: Only their direction matches, not their distance.

options.label: They are the same age
options.rationale: Nothing about a constellation implies that.

questions.explanation: A constellation is a pattern seen from Earth. Stars in it can be at very different distances and just happen to line up from our viewpoint.

questions.prompt: From Level 8: two stars in Orion are 50 and 500 light-years away. What does that mean for their light?

options.label: Their light reaches us at the same moment it leaves
options.rationale: Light takes time to travel: one year per light-year.

options.label: The farther star’s light is 10 times brighter
options.rationale: Distance says nothing about how bright a star is.

options.label: Both lights left them 500 years ago
options.rationale: Each star’s light left it a different time ago.

options.label: The farther star’s light left it about 450 years earlier

questions.explanation: A light-year is how far light travels in a year. Light from a star 500 light-years away left it about 500 years ago; from 50 light-years, about 50 years ago.
